compliance_risks.could_misstate: Classifying any product from its name. Doing so produces errors in both directions - calling insurance a membership, and calling a service a discount.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Never type or describe a product from its name. Read the Info page.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: Nothing client-facing. This is an internal rule.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: Product names in this portfolio are unreliable indicators of product type IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. 'AWA SimpleShield Membership Plan' is fixed indemnity insurance. 'Prime Health Pass Discount' is described on its own page as a Diagnostic Services Product delivering services. Between April and September NEO inserted the word 'Membership' into four Safe Guard product names without any evident change of type. Meanwhile 'AssistPro Discount' genuinely is a discount program.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Before any add-on is described on a call, and before any tooling assigns it a category.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Nothing directly - this is a defect in the document, not in what the agent says. But it means the clause telling the client who to contact about claims may be unreadable, and the client may later say they were never told who their agent was.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not tell a client the agreement names their agent.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: Give the client your own name, agency and email verbally on the recorded call, and confirm you are their contact for benefit and claims questions. Do not rely on the agreement to have done it.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: The FirstEnroll enrollment-agreement template served on the live storefront contains unrendered variables - $parentcompany, $product_label, $agent_fullname, $agent_Email, $parentemail - confirmed on two unrelated product families (American Financial Critical Illness page 38175, and Health Choice Silver page 32339). The affected clauses are the third-party administrator disclaimer, the Plan and Claims Inquiries clause and the Writing Agent Contact block.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Raise with FirstEnroll whether the executed enrollment document renders these variables. See G-039.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: For any product in this group, do not answer a coverage, exclusion, waiting-period or pre-existing question on a recorded call from portal material alone. Obtain the carrier document first.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: 51 of the 80 products on the NEO agent storefront have no brochure, certificate or policy document attached anywhere in the enrolment system. For those products the NEO reference page is the only available source, and four of those pages carry a limitations or exclusions heading with no text beneath it.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: Until the PDFs are filed, any compliance challenge to a benefit statement on these products can be answered only with the ledger's citations, not with the underlying document. Treat filing them as outstanding remediation, not housekeeping.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: Ten of the eleven linked brochures are READ and fully extracted into the ledger, but the PDF files themselves are not in Drive. The documents behind 25 live variants therefore exist in this project only as extracted facts, not as retrievable source documents.

dependent_rules.sec: SEC 2 DEFINITIONS - 2.21.4 Eligible Dependents and 2.22 Dependent (continues p.7)
dependent_rules.v: A child of a covered Eligible Employee who has not attained age 26 is an Eligible Dependent (biological child, stepchild, legally adopted child, or foster child placed by court order). Coverage for a Dependent Child continues until the end of the calendar month he or she turns 26. An Employee's Child, regardless of age, who is mentally or physically incapable of sustaining his or her own living may continue if written proof is furnished within 31 days after the limiting age. Active-duty members of any armed force and residents of a country other than the United States shall not be deemed Dependents.

excluded_services.v: The following exclusions apply to the benefits offered under this Plan: (1) Office visits, physical examinations, immunizations, and tests when required solely for sports, camp, employment, travel, insurance, marriage, or legal proceedings; (2) Routine foot care for treatment of flat feet, corns, bunions, calluses, toenails, fallen arches, weak feet, or chronic foot strain; (3) Dental procedures; (4) Any other medical service, treatment, or procedure not covered under this Plan; (5) Any other expense, bill, charge, or monetary obligation not covered under this Plan, including but not limited to all non-medical service expenses, bills, charges, and monetary obligations. Unless the medical service is explicitly provided by this Appendix A or otherwise explicitly provided in this Plan Document, this Plan does not cover the medical service or any related expense, bill, charge, or monetary obligation to the medical service; (6) Claims unrelated to treatment of medical care or treatment; (7) Cosmetic surgery unless authorized as medically necessary. Such authorization is based on the following causes for cosmetic surgery: accidental injury, correction of congenital deformity within six (6) years of birth, or as a treatment of a diseased condition; (8) Any treatment with respect to treatment of teeth or periodontium, any treatment of periodontal or periapical disease involving teeth surrounding tissue, or structure. Exceptions to this exclusion include only malignant tumors or benefits specifically noted in the schedule of benefits to the Plan Document; (9) Any claim related to an injury arising out of or in the course of any employment for wage or profit; (10) Claims which would otherwise be covered by a Worker's Compensation policy for which a participant is entitled to benefit; (11) Any claim arising from service received outside of the United States, except for the reasonable cost of claims billed by the Veterans Administration or Department of Defense for benefits covered under this Plan and not incurred during or from service in the Armed Forces of the United States; (12) Claims for which a participant is not legally required to pay or claims which would not have been made if this Plan had not existed; (13) Claims for services which are not medically necessary as determined by this Plan or the excess of any claim above reasonable and customary rates when a PPO network has not been contracted; (14) Charges which are or could be reimbursed by any public health program irrespective of whether such coverage has been elected by a participant; (15) Claims due to an act of war, declared or undeclared, not including acts of terrorism; (16) Claims for eyeglasses, contacts, hearing aids (or examinations for the fitting thereof) or radial keratotomy; (17) Abortion Services; (18) Travel, unless specifically provided in the schedule of benefits; (19) Custodial care for primarily personal, not medical, needs provided by persons with no special medical training or skill; (20) Claims from any provider other than a healthcare provider as defined in the Plan Document unless explicitly permitted in the schedule of benefits; (21) Investigatory or experimental treatment, services, or supplies unless specifically covered under Approved Clinical Trials; (22) Services or supplies which are primarily educational; (23) Claims due to attempted suicide or intentionally self-inflicted injury while sane or insane, unless the claim results from a medical condition such as depression; (24) Claims resulting from, or which arise due to the attempt or commission of, an illegal act. Claims by victims of domestic violence will not be subject to this exclusion; (25) Claims with respect to any treatment or procedure to change one's physical anatomy to those of the opposite sex and any other treatment or study related to sex change; (26) Claims from a medical service provider who is related by blood, marriage, or legal adoption to a participant; (27) Any claims for fertility or infertility treatment; (28) Claims for weight control, weight reduction, or surgical treatment for obesity or morbid obesity, unless explicitly provided in the schedule of benefits; (29) Claims for disability resulting from reversal of sterilization; (30) Claims for the completion of forms, or failure to keep scheduled appointments; (31) Recreational or diversional therapy; (32) Personal hygiene or convenience items, including but not limited to air conditioning, humidifiers, hot tubs, whirlpools, or exercise equipment, irrespective of the recommendations or prescriptions of a medical service provider; (33) Claims due to participation in a dangerous activity, including but not limited to sky-diving, motorcycle or automobile racing, bungee jumping, rock climbing, rappelling, or hang gliding; (34) Claims that arise primarily due to medical tourism; (35) Supportive devices of the foot; (36) Treatments for sexual dysfunction; (37) Aquatic or massage therapy; (38) Biofeedback training; (39) Skilled nursing facilities; (40) Durable medical equipment and prosthetics; (41) Hospice care, private duty nursing, or long-term care; (42) Residential facility - for charges from a residential halfway house or home, or any facility which is not a health care institution licensed for the primary purpose of treatment of an illness or injury; (43) Claims for temporomandibular joint syndrome; (44) Claims for biotech or specialty prescriptions; (45) Any claim which is not explicitly covered in the schedule of benefits; (46) Genetic testing unless explicitly covered in the schedule of benefits; (47) Organ transplants; (48) Claims for cosmetic surgery, not related to mastectomy reconstruction to produce a symmetrical appearance or prosthesis, or physical complications which result from such procedures; (49) Chiropractic care; (50) Radiation and chemotherapy; (51) Dialysis; (52) Acupuncture; (53) Alternative medicine/homeopathy; (54) Children dental and vision; (55) Neonatal intensive care (NICU); (56) Rehabilitative therapies; (57) PCP surgery; (58) Routine eye care (Adult); (59) Non-emergency care when traveling outside the U.S.; (60) Pregnancy Benefits, including office visits and childbirth/delivery professional and facility services; (61) Routine well-baby care of newborn infant while inpatient. The purpose of this list of exclusions is solely to provide additional clarity regarding treatments, procedures, products, services, or any other items which are not covered under this plan. Accordingly, no exclusion shall be interpreted by negative implication, or otherwise, as evidence of the existence of coverage under this plan.
